title: JZ-motion: explainers, fast (about this app, with edit demo)

elements.text: an LLM-first studio for explainer videos

beats.title: Logo
beats.notes:
Hi, it's Jakub here
and today I will share with you my latest app - JZ motion.

beats.title: What it is
beats.notes:
LLM first - explainer video creator.

Everything you'll see here was produced by it including a glowing marker board, animations, text, and charts.

beats.title: The usual tools
beats.notes: No Photoshop, After Effects or Premiere –

beats.title: What I use instead
beats.notes: just me, Claude Code and my app.

beats.title: Home
beats.notes: Creating explainer videos starts like a chat. One box in the middle of the screen.

beats.title: Just a sentence
beats.notes: I type what I want to explain, one sentence is enough, and a model drafts the whole presentation: scenes, drawings, beats and speaker notes.

beats.title: Three ways in
beats.notes: I can start from a topic, from a script I already wrote, or from a recording: then it transcribes me and cues every beat to the moment I say it.

beats.title: A model per job
beats.notes: And each way of starting can use a different model. More on why that matters in a minute.

beats.title: One box
beats.notes: So where does a video start? With one box, and one sentence about what I want to explain.

beats.title: A sentence
beats.notes: Here I'm asking for an explainer about this very app: how one sentence becomes a video.

beats.title: Three ways in
beats.notes: That sentence is a topic. I could paste a script I've already written instead, or upload a recording of me talking it through, and every beat gets cued to the moment I say it.

beats.title: Watch it work
beats.notes: The model I picked writes it, and every step is on screen: what was asked, what came back, and what the checker found.

beats.title: A first draft
beats.notes: A minute later there's a first draft: scenes, drawings, beats and speaker notes. Not finished, but something to react to, and that's the hard part done.

beats.title: The editor
beats.notes: The draft opens in the editor. One window: the board in the middle, scenes and the library on the left, properties on the right.

beats.title: The board
beats.notes: The board itself is the drawing surface. Everything on it is written, drawn, or placed by me or by the AI.

beats.title: Beats under it
beats.notes: Under the board is the storyboard. Each card is a beat: one click while I present, with its actions laid out on a small timeline.

beats.title: Properties on the right
beats.notes: Everything has properties — positions and sizes like a drawing program, colours as marker tips, styles as little pictures.

beats.title: Scenes and library on the left
beats.notes: I am able to inspect the list of scenes, and under it the library — icons, clipart, 3D models I can drop onto the board.

beats.title: A real recording
beats.notes: Now a closer look at editing. This is a real recording of the app, and I'm stepping through it one frame at a time, in step with what I say.

beats.title: Select
beats.notes: One click selects the headline, and its properties open on the right, with the marker it's drawn in lifted up.

beats.title: Recolour
beats.notes: Pick another marker, and the text is redrawn in that ink. Yellow. Or pink.

beats.title: Rewrite
beats.notes: A double-click opens the text right where it is. I type the new words, press Enter, and they're written in the same hand.

beats.title: Made by the app
beats.notes: And this clip was made by the app itself: a short script clicks through the editor, and the recording lands in the media library, sharp enough to zoom into.

beats.title: LLM first
beats.notes: Under the hood, jz-motion is designed to be LLM first.

beats.title: Context
beats.notes:
A presentation is not pixels: it's one JSON document.

Every request sends the model the format reference, the drawing rules and the whole library: every icon, logo, clipart and 3D model it may use.

beats.title: Schema check
beats.notes: LLM generated JSON is then being sent to schema checker to ensure that results are correct.

beats.title: Repair
beats.notes: …and if anything is wrong, the exact errors go back to the model to fix. That loop is why even small, cheap models produce something that loads.

beats.title: Board
beats.notes: Only valid JSON reaches the board, and from there it's all deterministic drawing.

beats.title: The JSON
beats.notes: And because it's plain JSON, I can read it, diff it, keep it in git, or edit it by hand.

elements.text: six marker colours · one stroke · drawn in order

beats.title: Same markers
beats.notes: The other goal is consistency. Whatever a model makes has to look like it came from the same set of markers.

beats.title: Everything
beats.notes: Icons, clipart, isometric 3D, charts, text: the same six colours, the same stroke, drawn in the order a person would draw them.

beats.title: Six marker colours
beats.notes: Green, pink, yellow, cyan, orange, white. Two to four per scene, each with a consistent meaning.

beats.title: Make your own
beats.notes: When the library doesn't have something, I describe it, and the model draws it under the same rules. The rules are shown, and every reply is checked.

beats.title: Versions
beats.notes: It's a conversation: every reply is a version. 'Make it pink', 'add a fan on top'… until I like one.

beats.title: Keep it
beats.notes: Then I save it, and from then on it's part of the library, for me and for every model that writes a presentation.

elements.text:
one source of truth —
so the house style stays the same

beats.title: One folder of skills
beats.notes: The skills folder is where I keep the rules: how to make a presentation, how to change one, how to draw a library item, how to demo an interface, how to turn it into a video.

beats.title: Both AIs follow them
beats.notes: The AI inside the app reads these files; Claude Code outside the app reads them too. So whichever one writes a scene, the style stays the same.

beats.title: One source of truth
beats.notes: Change the skill, change the output — on either side. That's how consistency survives.

scenes.title: A library that lowers the cost

beats.title: A shelf of pieces
beats.notes: The library is the shelf of pieces every explainer draws from: icons, logos, hand-drawn clipart, 3D models — every one checked against the house style.

beats.title: Each explainer adds one
beats.notes: When a presentation needs something new, I describe it, the model draws it under the same rules, and it joins the shelf.

beats.title: So each one costs less
beats.notes: Reusing is free; generating costs tokens. More in the library means fewer new items each time — and every explainer costs less than the one before.

beats.title: Overview
beats.notes: Here's how it fits together.

beats.title: In the browser
beats.notes:
In the browser, we have frontend application made with React.

SVG animations are made with GSAP

3d coordinates are calculated with 3JS

beats.title: A small local server
beats.notes:
paired with local server responsible for: 
keeping the files, 
proxying LLM calls,
transcription of recordings, 
and export of videos.

beats.title: Swappable models
beats.notes: The LLM is swappable: Claude, or anything OpenAI-compatible through OpenRouter, my own GPUs, or Ollama locally.

beats.title: Voice both ways
beats.notes: Although I used my own recording here - Voice goes both ways: an OpenAI TTS model generates narration from the script; an OpenAI transcription model turns a recorded script back into timed text.

scenes.title: The right model for each job

beats.title: Right job
beats.notes: Because every request is checked and repaired, I can experiment with smaller models.

beats.title: Story
beats.notes: A strong model writes the story: the structure, the scenes, the words.

beats.title: Small edits
beats.notes: Small edits, like changing a beat, work fine with a fast, cheap models like Haiku.

beats.title: Drawings
beats.notes: Icons, charts and 3D models are small, strict JSON. Haiku plus the rules is enough, and the library means most are never generated twice.

beats.title: Voice
beats.notes: I have used small OpenAI models for text-to-speech & transcription. Let me just add that I am using text to speach just for timing purposes - I have recorded final voice over myself.

beats.title: Transcription
beats.notes: And when I record myself talking, Whisper transcribes it, so I can start a whole presentation from a recording — scenes cued to the moments I spoke.

beats.title: Script at the centre
beats.notes: The script is the centre of this app. Every scene, every beat, every spoken sentence lives in one place.

beats.title: Three ways to touch it
beats.notes:
I can read and edit the whole thing in the Script view, 

inline in the Timing prompter, 

or in the raw JSON tab if I want to see the shape.

beats.title: Same text, three lenses
beats.notes: I have three views on the same text. so that I can pick whichever one fits what I'm doing right now.

beats.title: The prompter
beats.notes: Once presentation is ready I can move to the Timing window in prompter mode.

beats.title: Each sentence, its own line
beats.notes:
Every sentence of the beat shows on its own line, big and readable from a distance. 

I don't lose my pace when I look up at the camera.

beats.title: A target time per line
beats.notes: Next to each sentence, its target duration — pulled from a short voice clip the text-to-speech model generates. I know exactly how long each line should take.

beats.title: A clock that keeps me honest
beats.notes: At the bottom, a timeline shows where I am in the whole thing. The playhead moves as I read; a glance tells me if I'm fast, slow, or on it.

beats.title: Just read
beats.notes: Pull back and press record. No guessing the pace, no re-doing takes because I rushed one beat — I just read.

beats.title: Timing
beats.notes: When the words are right, I open Timing. It starts on the scene I was working on, and the script turns into a prompter.

beats.title: One line at a time
beats.notes: Each sentence sits on its own line, large enough to read from across the room, with the time it should take beside it.

beats.title: The timeline
beats.notes: Underneath is the timeline: my voice on two lanes, and every beat placed on it. Drag a beat, and that's the moment it appears in the video.

beats.title: Just read
beats.notes: To record, I press Record and read. The arrow key moves on to the next line, and every beat lands exactly where I said it.

beats.title: Tidy up
beats.notes: If a take is noisy, one click cleans up the voice. If I want the words back, it transcribes them for me.

beats.title: AI, wherever I am
beats.notes: The AI isn't a single feature here — it's everywhere in the app. It's in the home screen, inside the editor, in the library & in timing screen

beats.title: A sentence to a draft
beats.notes: From the home screen I pick a mode — topic, script, or recording — and a model, and go from one sentence to a whole first draft.

beats.title: Change THIS scene
beats.notes: Inside the editor, every scene has an ask bar above the storyboard. Describe one change — 'split this beat', 'add a database' — and only that scene changes.

beats.title: Chat about the whole thing
beats.notes: And on the AI tab in the right panel, a chat for bigger changes — picking models, running agent mode, watching every step land in the file.

beats.title: Same skills everywhere
beats.notes: All of them have access to the same skills. Pick the place that fits the move — the house style follows.

beats.title: Everywhere
beats.notes: The AI isn't one button in the corner. It's wherever I happen to be working.

beats.title: Home
beats.notes: On the home screen, it turns a sentence into a first draft.

beats.title: This scene
beats.notes: In the editor, the bar above the beats changes just this scene: split a beat, add a database, or, like here, turn one part into a scene of its own.

beats.title: The AI tab
beats.notes: The AI tab is for bigger conversations about the whole presentation, and I can watch each step as it edits the file.

beats.title: The library
beats.notes: And in the library, I describe a picture I'm missing, and it's drawn in the same marker style.

beats.title: Same skills
beats.notes: Every one of them reads the same skills, so whichever I reach for, the result looks like it belongs.

elements.text: for a 10-minute video, start to finish

beats.title: The number
beats.notes: One of main goals was to create an app that would allow me to create a ten-minute explainer under five dollars. I am happy to share that I was successful.

beats.title: Why it works
Record
beats.notes:
And the last mile: I click Record and adjusting the timeing, like I'm doing now. My script, my voice, and every click are saved as a take.

Thank you for watching

beats.title: Export
beats.notes: It exports straight to an MP4, with my camera in the corner or side by side with a friend. Or I record first, and it builds the presentation from the transcript.

beats.title: Thanks
beats.notes: That's jz-motion: explainers in minutes, in one consistent style, a little cheaper every time. Thanks for watching.
